title: Frankincense and myrrh reed diffuser
subtitle: A slow-release room fragrance with warm, resinous depth
excerpt: Frankincense and myrrh reed diffuser is a slow-release room fragrance made from frankincense and myrrh essential oils in a dipropylene glycol carrier, set with rattan reeds in a small open bottle. The resins give a warm, smoky, woody character that develops over several days. Makes enough for a 50 ml bottle; scents a small to medium room for six to eight weeks.
sourceNotes: Reed diffuser formulation using DPG (dipropylene glycol) as a carrier: RIFM (Research Institute for Fragrance Materials) technical bulletin on reed diffuser bases (2019). DPG is a standard reed diffuser carrier because it wicks easily, evaporates slowly, and carries fragrance effectively without being flammable at room temperature. Frankincense (Boswellia carterii) and myrrh (Commiphora myrrha) essential oil blend ratio adapted from The Complete Book of Essential Oils and Aromatherapy by Valerie Wormwood (1991).

recipe.yieldDescription: 50 ml reed diffuser (6 to 8 weeks of fragrance)
recipe.batchNotes: Fill multiple bottles from a larger batch. Keep the essential oil percentage at 20 to 25% of the total volume for reed diffuser use.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Ready to use immediately. The fragrance develops fully over the first three to four days as the reeds saturate.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: The diffuser runs for six to eight weeks before the fragrance fades. The base oil itself keeps 14 months sealed, refill the bottle rather than replacing it. Discard the reeds when they stop wicking (typically after one refill).

glossaryTerms.definition: A colourless, odourless carrier liquid used as the base for reed diffusers. It has a low evaporation rate, wicks readily up rattan reeds, and carries fragrance oils without flash-point concerns. Non-flammable at room temperature.

content.text: Combine the DPG and essential oils in the diffuser bottle. Stir or gently swirl to mix. Insert three to five rattan reeds. Flip the reeds after 30 minutes to accelerate the initial wicking. Leave in a stable position away from drafts.

More reeds give a stronger throw; fewer give a subtler background note. Flip all reeds every one to two weeks to refresh the throw as the dry ends slow down wicking. Replace the reeds when they stop wicking even after flipping, usually after one refill.
Frankincense and myrrh essential oils should be used with caution in rooms where cats or birds spend extended time. Keep diffusers out of reach of pets and in well-ventilated rooms.

The diffuser runs for six to eight weeks. Top up with a fresh 50 ml batch of the same formula rather than replacing the bottle. Discard the reed set after the first refill, saturated reeds gradually lose their wicking ability.
